Using 'shell=True' with subprocess can lead to shell injection vulnerabilities. Instead, use a list to pass arguments: subprocess.run(['ping', '-c', '1', host], capture_output=True).
Fetching each customer individually in a loop can lead to performance issues due to multiple database calls. Consider fetching all customers in a single query as was done previously.
Using a list for 'seen' results in O(n^2) time complexity for checking duplicates. Consider using a set for 'seen' to improve performance to O(n).

The 'signup' function is hardcoding the role as 'member'. This may not be appropriate for all use cases. Consider passing the role as a parameter to the function.

Sorting the items in place can be inefficient for large lists. Consider using 'sorted(items, key=lambda item: item['price'])' to return a new sorted list instead.

The signup function does not handle cases where 'name' or 'email' might not be present in the request. Add validation to ensure these keys exist before accessing them.
The create_user function should validate the role parameter to ensure it is one of the expected values (e.g., 'member', 'admin'). Add validation logic to handle unexpected role values.

The code assumes that every item has a 'price' key. If any item does not have this key, it will raise a KeyError. Consider adding error handling to manage items without a 'price' key.
